headline: A preprint reports black-box audits for undisclosed output-token inflation in LLM services
summary: Chen et al. define provider-side token inflation attacks as undisclosed provider-controlled changes that increase returned, billable output while largely preserving task utility. They instantiate five attack paths and report output lengths above 10.2 times a clean baseline. Their saturation-based probe achieves 85.1% macro q-AUC with false-positive rates below 2% across four open-weight models. In a black-box audit of 15 API services, they flag seven as showing behavior consistent with the attack. These are author-reported preprint results: a flag does not prove manipulation or dishonest intent, and broader prevalence is unknown.
